newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close sharply higher-limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close sharply higher-limit up.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed sharply higher to the three-cent limit up aided by rising prices in the cash market and fund buying, traders said.

They said E.D.& F. Man International was the major buyer of August bellies on the day with ING also featured on the buy-side. August ended the day bid the three cent limit up at 85.425 cents with the pool of unfilled buy-orders estimated at 175 cars.
They noted USDA reported at midday that cash bellies had traded as high as $92.00 per cwt for 12-14 lb supplies, a rise of $8.00 since the end of last week.

Dealers said the cash market looked poised to rise further with talk already circulating of trade at $93.00. The recent comparatively small hog kills and a seasonal pick-up in demand for bacon has helped to raise prices in the cash market.
Short covering ahead of Friday's USDA cold storage also helped to support values.
Analysts' estimates for frozen belly stocks, as of July 1, ranged from 53.5 to 53.8 million lbs, down from 55.274 million a year earlier.
Hog futures closed mostly higher, aided by firming product prices in fairly quiet conditions.
Floor sources said R.J. O'Brien had been the biggest buyer of August hogs, which closed up 0.175 cent at 80.825 cents.
Other months were up 0.250 cent to off 0.075 cent.

Gains were established despite weakness in cash hogs, with prices $0.50 to $1.00 lower on Thursday at the key Iowa-south Minnesota interior market. Cash hogs were expected to be steady to about $0.50 lower on Friday.
